newsitem.title: FRANCE: Shevardnadze rules out NATO bid for Georgia.
newsitem.headline: Shevardnadze rules out NATO bid for Georgia.

text.p: Georgian President Eduard Shevardnadze, on a visit to France, said on Monday it would be unrealistic for the former Soviet republic to apply for NATO membership but still hoped to join the European Union.
The Georgian leader told reporters after lunch with French President Jacques Chirac that rather than the proposed enlargement of the Atlantic Alliance he would have preferred an expansion of the EU.
"Even if Georgia applied for NATO membership, no one would consider this seriously," he said.
Chirac said France wanted to have an active role in the Caucasus which he said was part of Europe.
He said his talks with Shevardnadze, whom he described as a long-time friend, covered ways to strengthen Georgia's ties with France and Europe.

Diplomats said French leaders would tell Shevardnadze they back Georgia's bid to join the 40-member Council of Europe, which monitors democracy on the continent, and wanted early ratification of the 1996 partnership agreement between the European Union and Georgia.
Shevardnadze, who has been warmly praised by French authorities for democratic and economic reforms, was in France for a three-day official visit.
He was due to meet Foreign Minister Herve de Charette later on Monday and French business leaders on Tuesday.
